basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 50.' and it opens '(Vers. 50 et seqq.) Et Joseph nati sunt duo filii antequam venirent anni famis, quos'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 50 et seqq.) Et Joseph nati sunt duo filii antequam venirent anni famis, quos peperit ei Aseneth filia Phutipharis sacerdotis Heliopoleos. Vocavit autem Joseph nomen primogeniti Manasse: quia oblivisci me fecit Deus omnium laborum meorum, et omnis domus patris mei. Nomen autem secundi vocavit Ephraim, quia crescere me fecit Deus in terra humilitatis meae. Observa propter quaestionem, quae post paululum de Joseph filiis proponenda est, quod ante famis tempus, quo Jacob intravit in Aegyptum, duos tantum Joseph filios habuerit, Manasse et Ephraim. Manasse vocans ab eo, quod sit oblitus laborum suorum: ita enim Hebraice vocatur oblivio. Ephraim, eo quod auxerit eum Deus. Et ex hoc enim vocabulo in linguam nostram transfertur augmentum.
